headline: D12 Sturm engine consumed with constructed D10 Jacobi data; literal acceptance branch (1) refuted and replaced by the offered sharper two-curvature interlacing; zero-counting/first-zero bound and Wronskian consumption delivered; all gates PASS.

honest_classification.item_1_literal: REFUTED (k2=0,u2=t cannot instantiate the engine; sin has no zero in (0,pi); first positive zero is exactly pi)
honest_classification.item_1_alternative: DELIVERED (general strict-gap interlacing + explicit sin vs k2=1/2 instance)
honest_classification.item_2: DELIVERED (closed-interval zero incl. equality case, firstPositiveZero <= pi/sqrt K, horizon form, cross-checked against conjugate_point_bound)
honest_classification.item_3: DELIVERED (wronskian_antitoneOn_of_le and wronskian_deriv with explicit (1,sin)/(0,t) data; t*cos t <= sin t)

semantic_class: unconditional scalar ODE comparison (Sturm). No manifold-level Jacobi field, conjugate point, Rauch or Poincare statement is claimed.

constructed_data.linearJacobiSolutionOn: (fun _ => 0, fun t => t, fun _ => 1, fun _ => 0) is a JacobiSolutionOn (0,T)

constructed_data.first_zero_values: jacobiSol K (K>0) has least positive zero pi/sqrt K (firstPositiveZero_modelJacobiSol); Real.sin has least positive zero pi (firstPositiveZero_sin).

acceptance_items.item: (1) engine instantiated with k1=1 (u1=sin) and k2=0 (u2=t) on (0,pi), OR the sharper two-curvature interlacing for k2 <= k1
literal_form_analysis: sturm_zero_comparison requires u2 b = 0. For (k2,u2)=(0, t) and any 0 < b we have u2 b = b != 0 (linear_model_no_second_zero), so the engine is structurally inapplicable on any interval with positive right endpoint.

The would-be conclusion 'first positive zero of sin is < pi' is false: sin has no zero in (0,pi) and its first positive zero is exactly pi (sin_first_positive_zero_is_pi).  The refutation lemma sin_no_zero_in_Ioo_zero_pi is the read-only prior art from SturmZeroCount.lean, reused by name and not reproved here.
The data (k2,u2)=(0,t) is instead consumed through the Wronskian route, yielding the true inequality t*cos t <= sin t on [0,pi] (mul_cos_le_sin).
delivered_alternative: exists_zero_of_curvature_lt: general two-curvature interlacing: k2 <= k1 on [a,b], u2(a)=u2(b)=0, u2>0 on (a,b), u1(a)=0, and k2 t0 < k1 t0 somewhere in (a,b) => u1 has a zero in (a,b).
sin_zero_interlaces_half_model: explicit instance k1=1 (u1=sin), k2=1/2 (u2=jacobiSol (1/2)), consecutive model zeros 0 and pi/sqrt(1/2)=sqrt(2)*pi bracket the explicit zero pi of sin.
sin_first_zero_lt_half_model_first_zero: strict first-zero ordering pi < sqrt(2)*pi.

sin_interlaces_half_model_all: for every n : Int, sin has a zero strictly between the consecutive zeros 2*n*pi and 2*(n+1)*pi of the shifted model jacobiSolShift (1/4) (2*n*pi) (curvature k2=1/4); the zeros interlace on every period.
sin_zero_in_half_model_interval: the explicit witness (2n+1)*pi is a zero of sin in that interval, for every n : Int.

firstPositiveZero_lt_of_curvature_lt: the first-zero ordering form of the same interlacing: under the hypotheses above, firstPositiveZero u1 < b, i.e. the higher-curvature solution has its first positive zero strictly before the first zero b of the lower-curvature solution.

firstPositiveZero_modelJacobiSol / firstPositiveZero_sin / firstPositiveZero_sin_lt_half_model: the two first zeros are computed in closed form (pi/sqrt K and pi) and the explicit ordering firstPositiveZero Real.sin < firstPositiveZero (jacobiSol (1/2)), i.e. pi < sqrt(2)*pi, is proved.

sin_zero_linear_zeroFree_interlacing: the honest degenerate statement for the literal (k1,u1)=(1,sin), (k2,u2)=(0,t) data: t is zero-free on (0,pi] while sin has the zero pi there, so the higher-curvature solution's zero precedes every positive zero of the lower-curvature one.

acceptance_items.item: (2) zero-counting corollary: for K>0, k>=K, the first positive zero of a Jacobi solution with u 0=0, u' 0=1 (if it exists before a given horizon) is at most pi/sqrt(K), cross-checked against this round's conjugate_point_bound
delivered: exists_jacobi_zero_on_Ioc_pi_sqrt: k>=K on [0,pi/sqrt K], u 0=0 => exists zero in (0, pi/sqrt K].
eq_zero_at_pi_sqrt_of_curvature_eq: equality-case endpoint zero via Wronskian constancy (upgrades the engine's open-interval alternative to the closed-interval statement).
exists_jacobi_zero_on_Ioc_pi_sqrt_of_interior_bound: the ODE-intrinsic form of the closed-interval zero, with the curvature bound required only on the open interval (0, pi/sqrt K).
exists_jacobi_zero_on_Ioc_pi_sqrt_normalized: same with the normalization hypothesis u' 0 = 1 recorded.
exists_jacobi_zero_of_horizon: horizon form: solution known on (0,H) with H >= pi/sqrt K has a zero in (0, pi/sqrt K].

firstPositiveZero_le_pi_sqrt_of_horizon: horizon form of the first-zero bound, matching the acceptance wording 'if it exists before a given horizon': data on (0,H) with H >= pi/sqrt K gives firstPositiveZero u <= pi/sqrt K.
firstPositiveZero_le_pi_sqrt_of_interior_bound: the first-zero bound with the interior curvature hypothesis.
firstPositiveZero_le_pi_sqrt: firstPositiveZero u := sInf {t>0 | u t=0} satisfies firstPositiveZero u <= pi/sqrt K; the zero set is nonempty.
firstPositiveZero_jacobiSol_two: explicit non-vacuous witness k=2, K=1, u=jacobiSol 2, zero at pi/sqrt 2 <= pi/sqrt 1.
pos_near_zero_of_normalized_initial: with u' 0 = 1, u > 0 near 0 (FTC: u t = integral_0^t du and du > 1/2 near 0), so the zero set is bounded away from 0.

firstPositiveZero_mem_of_normalized: the infimum firstPositiveZero u is ATTAINED at a genuine zero: u (firstPositiveZero u) = 0, 0 < firstPositiveZero u, and u is zero-free in (0, firstPositiveZero u).
